trade claims in this estate are estimated at $200–$400 million (midpoint $300 million)

Given the active lift-stay motion practice and ongoing claims trading, a withdrawal of a lift-stay motion or a related objection is the most probable candidate, but that is unverified. At the scale of this estate — with confirmed plan value anchored to more than $1 billion in antitrust litigation — individual small-balance transfers carry no meaningful recovery impact, but the volume signals active secondary-market interest in Harvest Sherwood paper in the weeks immediately following confirmation.

The next concrete milestone is September 21, 2026, when trial begins in Adversary Proceeding 25-08002, Harvest Sherwood v. Sprouts Farmers Market, before Judge Jernigan. That proceeding is the most proximate litigation event bearing on estate recovery, and any pre-trial motion practice or stipulation filed before then will carry the highest near-term materiality.

items.body_md:
On August 7, the clerk docketed three separate relief-from-stay motions (Dkt. 1169, 1173, 1181) together with corresponding notices of hearing (Dkt. 1174, 1175, 1180) and a generic order (Dkt. 1168), the first material cluster of lift-stay activity since plan confirmation on August 5. The simultaneous filing of three distinct motions — each a separate creditor or counterparty seeking to liquidate claims outside the automatic stay — is not unusual at this stage of a confirmed liquidating plan, where the stay remains in place until the effective date but creditors with contingent claims against third-party insurers or co-defendants have reason to move promptly. The motions' subject matter, movants, and proposed hearing dates are not yet legible from the docket titles alone; the notices of hearing at Dkt. 1174, 1175, and 1180 will carry the scheduled dates, which are not yet reflected in the docket record provided.

Four claim assignments (Dkt. 1175–1178) were logged the same day via the claims agent, continuing the pattern of secondary-market trading in Harvest Sherwood claims that has run throughout the case. Two pro hac vice admissions (Dkt. 1170, 1171) also appeared August 7, indicating that at least one new firm or out-of-district practitioner entered an appearance around the time of the lift-stay filings — a pairing that may reflect counsel for one of the lift-stay movants, though that connection is not confirmed on the face of the docket. On August 8, Dkt. 1186 recorded a BNC certificate of mailing, the administrative confirmation that the August 7 notices went out to all scheduled recipients. 
Plan confirmation was entered at the August 5 hearing, where Judge Jernigan overruled the remaining U.S. Trustee objection
 — __[Law360](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy-authority/articles/2510100/harvest-sherwood-wins-ch-11-plan-approval)__ — so the lift-stay cluster landing two days later reflects the predictable post-confirmation sprint by parties needing stay relief before the plan goes effective.

The recovery posture for claimants is unchanged by this cluster: the confirmed plan's mechanism centers on 
maximizing value of more than $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims against more than 25 defendants across the chicken, pork, and beef producer industries
 — __[Atlas Grove/PRNewswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/atlas-grove-announces-court-approval-of-180-million-financing-commitment-for-harvest-sherwood-bankruptcy-estate-302821009.html)__ — with distributions flowing after that litigation trust is funded and operational. The lift-stay motions, if granted, would allow individual movants to pursue their own claims in other forums, which is recoverable neutral or marginally positive for the estate to the extent it reduces administrative claim exposure rather than extracting estate assets. The next concrete milestone is September 21, when the adversary proceeding against Sprouts Farmers Market (Adv. Pro. 25-08002) goes to trial before Judge Jernigan — the proceeding through which the estate is pursuing its damages claim arising from Sprouts' transition to self-distribution.

items.body_md:
Friday's docket is the heaviest single-day volume since plan confirmation on August 5, and its composition is structurally significant. Dkt. 1167 — an order confirming the Chapter 11 plan — marks the entry of the signed confirmation order, the instrument that formally converts the August 5 oral ruling into an operative, appealable judgment. That order is the gating document for plan effectiveness: until it is entered on the docket, conditions to effectiveness cannot begin running, distributions cannot be authorized, and the Liquidating Trust cannot be formally stood up. Its appearance on August 7, two days after the hearing, is routine timing and carries no negative inference, but claimants should now be tracking the conditions-to-effectiveness checklist against any outside dates specified in the confirmed plan — those clocks are now running.

Three separate relief-from-stay motions were filed on the same day — Dkts. 1169, 1173, and 1181 — each accompanied or preceded by a notice of hearing at Dkts. 1174, 1175, and 1180. Three lift-stay motions arriving simultaneously in the immediate aftermath of plan confirmation is not coincidental. The most common trigger at this stage of a liquidating case is a secured creditor or counterparty seeking to enforce against collateral or pursue litigation in another forum now that the plan framework has been set. The identity of the movants, the collateral or rights at issue, and the dollar exposure are not publicly confirmed from available sources; the hearing notices will establish the return dates. Claimants with overlapping collateral interests or co-obligor exposure should obtain the underlying motions to assess whether their recovery position is implicated before those hearings are reached.

Four additional claim assignments were processed through claims agent Epiq Corporate Restructuring, LLC at Dkts. 1175 through 1178 — extending what is now an eight-transfer run across three days following confirmation. The pace and concentration of these transfers, occurring in the 48-to-96-hour window after the confirmation order entered, continues to reflect secondary-market buyers underwriting recovery at a now-judicially-anchored price point. Two pro hac vice admissions at Dkts. 1170 and 1171 and a clerk's correspondence at Dkt. 1172 carry no immediate strategic weight. The next hard deadline with direct recovery consequence remains the adversary trial in *Harvest Sherwood v. Sprouts Farmers Market*, Adv. Pro. 25-08002, before Judge Jernigan on September 21, 2026 — the proceeding tied to 
Atlas Grove's position as plan funder, pursuing more than $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims against more than 25 defendants primarily across the chicken, pork, and beef producer industries
 (__[Yahoo Finance / PRNewswire](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/atlas-grove-announces-court-approval-164900571.html)__). Between now and September 21, the principal monitoring items are: satisfaction of plan effectiveness conditions now that Dkt. 1167 is entered, the return dates on the three lift-stay motions, and continued claim-transfer filings as secondary-market conviction on recovery quantum develops.

That clustering is not incidental: a now-confirmed plan provides the price-discovery anchor that secondary-market buyers need to underwrite claim acquisitions, and the volume here suggests at least two distinct purchasers are building or topping up positions in quick succession. Each transfer of record under Bankruptcy Rule 3001(e)(2) carries a 21-day notice period before the transferee can be substituted as holder; claimants monitoring their own claims should confirm whether any transfer notice implicates their position.

The compensation filing at Dkt. 1157 (August 6) — the day's only substantive administrative entry beyond the claim transfers and the pro hac vice admissions covered yesterday — continues the professional-fee cadence running parallel to McDermott Will & Schulte LLP's thirteenth monthly fee statement at Dkt. 1143 for the June 1 through June 30, 2026 period. The identity of the applicant at Dkt. 1157 is not yet confirmed from publicly available sources; the filing's recovery-posture relevance depends on whether it reflects estate professionals, plan-funder counsel, or a new entrant, and that question is worth tracking when the order comes through. The certificate at Dkt. 1163 (August 6) has no immediate strategic implication. Nothing filed today or yesterday alters the relief from stay motion at Dkt. 1162, which remains the most tactically interesting open item from August 6 — a creditor moving against collateral or a co-obligor with the plan framework now settled, but whose target and claim size are not yet publicly confirmed.

The next hard deadline with direct recovery consequence remains the adversary trial in *Harvest Sherwood v. Sprouts Farmers Market*, Adv. Pro. 25-08002, before Judge Jernigan on September 21, 2026, alongside 
Atlas Grove Management's position as plan funder, pursuing more than $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims against more than 25 defendants primarily across the chicken, pork, and beef producer industries
 (__[ABF Journal](https://www.abfjournal.com/atlas-grove-gains-court-approval-for-180mm-financing-commitment-for-harvest-sherwood-bankruptcy-estate/)__). Between now and September 21, the principal monitoring items are: the entry of the formal confirmation order (not yet docketed as a signed order in today's run), satisfaction of any conditions to plan effectiveness, and further claim-transfer filings that will continue to signal secondary-market conviction on the recovery quantum.
